findings.reason: The denominator noun is not pluralised, so a reachable count renders ungrammatical French: with one chat in the catalogue the footer reads « 1 sur 1 conversations » (and a search reads « 1 correspondance sur 1 conversations »); at 0 it reads « 0 sur 0 conversations ». French selects `one` for 0 and 1 and requires the singular noun, and at exact multiples of 10^6 it requires « de conversations ». The same sentence in ru, in this same PR, repairs it with a nested plural on {total}; fr does not. The two search messages also lack the `many` arm for the match noun, so 10^6 renders « 1000000 correspondances » instead of « 1 000 000 de correspondances ». The proposed strings were rendered with the repository's own formatter at 0/1/2/10^6 and produce « 1 sur 1 conversation », « 0 correspondance sur 0 conversation », « 1000000 de correspondances sur 1000000 de conversations ».

findings.reason: At an exact multiple of 10^6 the `other` arm renders « 1000000 agents intégrés », where French requires « d’agents intégrés »; 187 of the fr catalogue's 190 plural messages carry one/many/other, so this is a conformance gap, not a house style. It is a nit because the offer count is bounded by the packaged built-in profiles and the =0 arm is itself unreachable at the call site (availableBuiltins.length > 0 gates it), so no user can reach the count that exposes it.

verdict: changes_requested — 49/49 values read, 1 major (FR-FINAL-01, the unpluralised counter denominator, visible at 0/1 chats), 1 nit (FR-FINAL-02, the offer's missing many arm). The badge itself passes: 1 renders « 1 conversation dans ce groupe » and ::group-off is kept in every arm. Fixing FR-FINAL-01 changes the target hash and needs a one-value delta re-audit.

outside_scope_observations.observation: English uses `#`, so 1000 renders "1,000 chats in this group"; fr's required ::group-off renders "1000 conversations dans ce groupe". Recorded so a rendered check knows what to expect; not a fr defect and not changed here (the brief requires group-off).

The English source attaches a fixed plural noun to the total, so total=1 renders "Showing 1 of 1 chats". This PR briefly pluralised it in a2be7769e7 and reverted it in d784571d. English-side; fr must still repair its own noun (FR-FINAL-01), as ru already does.

chat-sidebar.tsx joins the names with " and " before passing them as {list}, so a French sentence shows "Alpha and Beta". The code comment states this as an ICU list-format limit, not an oversight; it is not a catalogue value and cannot be fixed in the fr file. Affects every locale.
